Supply Chain Consultancy

Supply chain consultancy that fixes the cause, not the symptom.

Your OTIF looks acceptable, but customers still complain. Stock keeps rising, yet the lines customers want are out. These are signs that the measure and the operation have drifted apart.

Signs you may need this

  • Service scores and customer experience tell different stories.
  • Inventory is growing faster than sales.
  • A small group of people spends most of the week firefighting exceptions.
  • Supplier reviews focus on last month’s delivery, not next year’s risk.
  • Planning, purchasing and warehouse teams each use their own numbers.

What I do

Using the JourneyIQ method, I map the order journey from customer promise to confirmed delivery. More inventory does not automatically mean better availability. The important question is where the constraint actually sits.

I measure where the promise changes, where stock waits and where manual work fills the gaps. From there, we agree the two or three changes that will move service and cash the most.

What you get

  • A single, agreed baseline for service, inventory and supplier performance
  • A clear view of where variability enters the chain
  • A short list of prioritised actions, each with an owner and a check date
  • Support to put the first actions in place, if you want it

Relevant evidence

OTIF moved from 60% to 85% across a 16-branch network in four months in a previous employed leadership role.

Questions

Do I need to send data before the first call?

No. The first conversation needs only a description of the problem.

How long does a diagnostic take?

Usually two to four weeks, depending on how easily the data can be accessed.

Do you work with small businesses?

Yes, if the operation is complex enough to benefit from an outside view, for example two or more sites or 1,000 or more active SKUs.
